analysis:
The PR gives the cluster-service supervisor (ClusterServiceCommand.swift:84-117, ClusterMemberSupervisor.swift) a coordinated pair-update path. The same supervisor holds the coordinator URL and auto_update gate from Watchdog.settings. It runs ClusterPairUpdateCycle, takes `darkbloom update` requests from a file (ClusterPairUpdate.takeRequest), and drains and SIGTERMs the service child via restartForUpdate (lines 510-519). It then runs the installed binary once as a start check (startCheckFailure, lines 589-595), execv's into it, and applies candidate promotion or rollback through ClusterCandidateRecovery (lines 531-584, 600-614).

I found no concrete regression in the supplied evidence. This is the TB-003 and T-043 area: rollback and update authority sits in the same replaceable provider binary. It touches TB-011 and T-053 only to the extent that the service restarts, because the update cycle ends in a service restart and the provider reconnects under a new process endpoint and authorization.

Observations for the next pass:
(1) Update authenticity (signature or hash verification, quarantine) lives in SelfUpdater and ClusterCandidateRecovery, which were not supplied. They are unchanged-in-kind but now run from a new route.
(2) The request file at requestPath is a local trigger. Its permissions and owner-only handling, and the ClusterPairUpdateCycle peer exchange between the Macs, are outside the supplied evidence.
(3) While `restarting` is set or the member is draining, the liveness guard is skipped (line 312) and no SIGKILL escalation is scheduled. A member that ignores SIGTERM could stall an update cycle; this is local availability only.
(4) endPairCycle awaits cycle.value after cancel (line 526), so a cycle that ignores cancellation could delay supervisor restarts.
(5) The lock fd is O_CLOEXEC, so execv releases it.
(6) StartCommand+ClusterMember.swift is patch metadata only. It adds clusterMemberAnswersUpdateDrain, whose consumption in ProviderLoop was not seen; this is a coordinator-visible drain behavior.

The start check runs the freshly installed binary as a child before execv. Its sandboxing and the integrity guarantees on the installed binary are unverified here.
